subject: Solid Waste and Composting Contract Proposal
overview: The committee reviewed a proposed 10-year solid waste contract that introduces citywide weekly food composting and a planned transition to bi-weekly trash collection in year three. DPW and Planning officials detailed fiscal strategies to offset rising costs, including new fees for bulky items and a preferred hauler program for business districts.

items.title: Overview of the Solid Waste RFP
items.summary: Commissioners presented a plan for a new 10-year contract with Waste Management focusing on cost control and zero-waste goals.

items.title: Proposed Weekly Food Composting and Bi-weekly Trash
items.summary: The proposal includes a weekly curbside composting service starting in 2024, followed by a transition to every-other-week trash collection in 2026 to save approximately $1 million annually.

items.title: Rodent Control and Waste Container Security
items.summary: Officials discussed using locking toters for food scraps to prevent rodent access, noting that these containers are more secure than standard trash bins currently in use.

items.title: Commercial District Waste and Preferred Hauler Program
items.summary: The city plans to transition small businesses toward a preferred hauler system with pre-negotiated rates to eliminate piles of loose trash bags in business squares.

items.title: Changes to Bulky Item and Yard Waste Collection
items.summary: The proposed contract introduces a nominal fee for bulky items to reduce service volume and extends yard waste collection through December using a bi-weekly alternating schedule.

items.title: Budget and Fiscal Impacts
items.summary: Councilors discussed the 3.5% to 6% projected annual budget growth for waste services and the long-term sustainability of funding these costs under state tax levy limits.
